description:
On-demand brain entry-point tool. Call this when you need to reach the brain mid-task — do NOT call it on every /aide boot. Boot-time brain precondition state is already reported by aide_info.brain.status; firing aide_brain at boot duplicates that work unnecessarily. It is also how a brain config is set up, repaired or written for any backend, one decision at a time. Every mode is read-only: no call writes to disk.

**Optional `source` parameter** — which read runs. Omitted means `"host"`.
- `"host"` — one section of the host's `.aide/config/brain.aide`, described below.
- `"template"` — `{ template, purpose }`: one section of the bundled template (or its launcher, with `kind: "launcher"`) as verbatim bytes, and that section's one-line purpose from the published contract. The answer is the same whatever state the host's config is in. Use it as a worked example when writing that section for another backend.
- `"contract"` — `{ sections }`: every contract section in order, each with `marker`, `role` (`live` or `seed`) and `purpose`, and no section text.
- `"draft"` — a structural check of the draft config at `path`, with the same rules and fault vocabulary as the host config check, so a draft that passes is ready to swap in. Returns `{ outcome, instructions }`: `valid`; `invalid` with `fault` (`missing-sections` and its `sections`, or `malformed` and its `reason`); `absent` when no file is at `path`; `refused` when `path` is outside the project, and nothing is read. It checks structure, never content.

**Optional `kind` parameter** — host and template reads only: any section marker of the published brain contract (see the enum), live or seed; `"launcher"` only with `source: "template"`. Omitting it means `"orientation"`, the runtime briefing for reaching the brain mid-task. `"config"` is the integration's wiring flow that `/aide:brain config` runs. Seed sections are fetched one per call while seeding. `path` is required with `source: "draft"` and accepted nowhere else; any other combination is rejected before the tool runs.

**Host read response shape: exactly `{ status, instructions, found, purpose? }`.** No `backend`, no `connector`, no `name`, no `kind`.

- `found: true` — `instructions` is that section's verbatim bytes from the host's `.aide/config/brain.aide`: no trimming, no normalization, no `${...}` substitution. `purpose` is that section's one-line purpose from the published contract; use it when adapting the section for another backend.
- `found: false` — `instructions` is remediation, and `purpose` is absent. An absent file → run `/aide:brain config`. A requested section missing from the file → with the user's consent, call `aide_upgrade` with `category: "brain"`. A malformed or unreadable file → the exact fault, a hand fix with the user, then re-check with `aide_info`. Do not proceed as if the section were available.

The section is returned on every status where the config exists and is well-formed, including `brain-aide-invalid` with missing sections, `no-mcp-entry` and `mcp-drift`.

`status` mirrors the `BrainState` tagged union from `buildBrainState`, with five values: `ok`, `no-brain-aide`, `brain-aide-invalid`, `no-mcp-entry`, `mcp-drift`. Branch on `found` for "did I get the section" and on `status` for "is the brain healthy".

kind.description: Which section: any section marker of the published contract, live or seed, or `launcher` with `source: "template"` only. Omitted means `orientation`. Not accepted with `contract` or `draft`. Seed sections are fetched one per call while seeding.

path.description: Project-relative path of a draft brain config. Required with `source: "draft"` and accepted nowhere else; a path outside the project is refused unread.

source.description: Which read runs. Omitted means `host`: one section of the host's `.aide/config/brain.aide`. `template`: one section or the launcher of the bundled template, with its purpose. `contract`: every contract section with its role and purpose. `draft`: a structural check of the draft config at `path`.

name: aide_brain
